context_needed: BRAC Targeting the Ultra Poor (TUP) programme, Rangpur, Kurigram and Nilphamari districts, Bangladesh. TUP1 = 1,997 households that qualified under BRAC's criteria and received the programme; TUP2 = 1,667 households that qualified but were not treated (p. 3). Rounds: 2002 (baseline) and 2005 (follow-up). Outcomes are multidimensional poverty measures built from normalised shortfalls (Eq. 1, p. 2): poverty gap (alpha=1), squared gap (alpha=2), cubic gap (alpha=3); the Bourguignon-Chakravarty block uses Eq. 2 with the theta and alpha printed above each column. Values are index points (0-1 scale); negative means poverty fell. Estimator: DiD with kernel propensity-score matching (Epanechnikov kernel, psmatch2; p. 3), estimand ATT. Table 2 is the main result (the highlights on p. 1 quote it as an 18-point fall); Table 3 holds robustness checks with changed weights, thresholds and index family.

rule: When a block shows the baseline gap, the follow-up difference and the difference-in-differences for the same outcome, store only the DiD row; the baseline gap and the follow-up difference are descriptive.
